models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light and benign overnight at Santa Marina; leave early tomorrow for Portorosa - thunderstorms threaten the afternoon.
briefing.synopsis: No organised gradient over the Aeolians - winds across all islands sit at 2-7 kt through tonight and tomorrow, backing and veering with the local diurnal pattern (ECMWF IFS 0.25°, AIFS and ICON-2i, all 08 Oct 12Z). At Salina the consensus is WSW 3.7 kt at midnight easing to 3.3 kt WSW by 06:00, then a light N/NE breeze filling around midday and an E'ly 5.8 kt by 18:00. The models carry a convective signal into tomorrow afternoon, with thunderstorms flagged in the 14:00-18:00 Salina-Portorosa window; seas build modestly from 0.7 ft tonight to 2.0 ft off Salina by tomorrow evening (MFWAM 08 Oct 00Z, cross-checked ECMWF WAM 12Z).
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Porto Santa Marina Salina is the recommendation and the clear pick - WSW 4.4 kt, gusts 12.8 kt, swell 0.5 ft from the SSE, which keeps both wind and sea out of the harbour's exposed 150-210° arc. Rinella also scores as sheltered (SE 3.7 kt, gusts 15.7 kt) but is open to the SE, so Santa Marina is the lower-fuss berth tonight. Nothing in the payload suggests the fleet would need to move; the trigger would be the breeze backing into the southern sector with any increase, which no model shows tonight. Note the 45.5 kt interval-maximum gust logged at Salina for 18:00 this evening - a single-model convective spike in a 3.4 kt mean, not a sustained wind, but a reminder to put lines and snubbers on properly.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Quiet start: Salina 06:00 shows WSW 3.3 kt, gusts 12.6 kt, 0.8 ft sea (consensus, 08 Oct 12Z runs). The recommended departure for Salina to Portorosa is 06:00, arriving about 10:00 - 3.3 kt WSW, gusts 13.8 kt, 0.8 ft seas, 82° TWA, so expect a beam reach on paper but plan on motoring. Conditions are rated go through a 12:00 start (arrive 16:00), with deterioration after 14:00; the 14:00 departure is marked no-go on thunderstorms. Take the early window and be alongside at Portorosa before the afternoon convection.

passage_notes.note: 06:00 start is the pick: WSW 3.3 kt, gusts 13.8 kt, 0.8 ft, arrive ~10:00. 10:00 start gives N 5.3 kt, gusts 16.5 kt, 1.1 ft dead downwind; 12:00 start NE 6.1 kt, gusts 20.4 kt, 1.7 ft. The 14:00 window is no-go - E 6.8 kt, gusts 25.1 kt, 1.9 ft, with thunderstorms forecast in the passage window. Light-air gust figures are interval maxima from IFS and ICON-2i, so they read high against the means.
Completed - all windows ran go, 3-7 kt and under 1 ft.

cautions: Thunderstorms are forecast in the 14:00-18:00 Salina-Portorosa window; convective gusts to 25.1 kt are shown against a 6.8 kt mean. Depart early rather than late.

Several very large gust figures (45.5 kt Salina 18:00 today, 37.3 kt Panarea, 36.3 kt Lipari) are interval maxima from a single model in near-calm air - treat them as showers/squall potential rather than sustained wind, but do not dismiss the convective signal.

With means of 2-7 kt the direction is effectively unreliable: the stability record shows a mean 40-43° direction shift at 0-24 h lead. Expect wind to come from somewhere other than forecast and plan on engines for most of the 24 nm.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i agree that the pattern is light - no models_range_kt flag appears at Salina for tonight or tomorrow morning - but at these wind speeds the direction is close to random (mean 40-43° shift run-to-run at 0-24 h), and the timing of tomorrow's thunderstorms is inherently low-confidence.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
